75.s: The band played Jazz from bought and traded arrangements including some from Benny Carter; Ramirez began orchestrating, studied harmony, and played bassoon at Commerce High School.
75.ch: Teens, stride pianists and the Louisiana Stompers
75.q: in those years, you know. Then we played "Chinatown". We used to buy them from the guy that... There were covers... And the big bands were selling them to the other bands. That was the big thing in those days. Then I had made a few. As soon as I learned to read... Boy, I read a book by Frank…

124.t: Arranging and head arrangements in the McRae band
124.s: William wrote for the band; sidemen learned arranging, and head arrangements worked out collectively often beat written ones.
124.ch: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
124.q: It was a lot of writing for those sections. Sometimes you'd have a trio, as you say, with a kind of different instrumentation, or with the use of a bass sax.

125.t: Learning to read and arrange: Lloyd Hunter, Nat Towles and Jim Bell's
125.s: Challenged, he studied reading and writing, moved to Lloyd Hunter and then Nat Towles, played Jim Bell's club in Omaha, and became a good arranger largely self-taught.
125.ch: Failure in St. Louis and the Omaha bands
125.q: Yes. I had been challenged and I had been encouraged to study more. Now, this all comes slowly and it came slowly. And I'm still studying music as most musicians do. So in my desire to better myself I realized that I had to study, so in the process I started to studying music more seriously, and…

78.t: Standard big-band instrumentation, writing for fiddles, and end of the proceedings
78.s: Horace wrote for the standard big-band instrumentation, a little for violins after studying at Damrosch in New York. The tape ends.
78.ch: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
78.q: -- like four trumpets, three trombones, five saxophones and everything. I wrote a little bit for fiddles, but I had to go to school a little bit. In fact, this is what you have to do. But mine was primarily like the instrumentation for the big bands, what they carried, originally had.

455.t: Rehearsing in St. Joseph; George E. Lee hears the band
455.s: The stranded band rehearses daily; George E. Lee hears them at the Frog Hop Ballroom and is scared by their arrangements.
455.ch: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
455.q: But I mean and some of the cats used to lay in bed all day rather than to give it up. So we were stranded. We used to rehearse every day. We had a great, great band, and I think I -- it was mentioned that this was when I first met Georgie Lee. He used to come in there, and they had opened up a…

13.t: Starting to arrange with Tate, and studying arranging with Sanborn
13.s: He began writing brass sections for Tate, then whole arrangements for Hines, and had studied arranging with Sanborn as a boy.
13.q: I started arranging when I was with Tate. I started arranging like Omer Simeon would arrange the saxaphone chords, I'd arrange the brass chords. They'd have what they called special courses. That's when I first started arranging.

112.t: Turned away by a white arranger; learning to write arrangements
112.s: A white arranging office changes its tone when it sees they are Black musicians, so Wooding begins writing whole arrangements himself.
112.q: : Well, I'll tell you Chris, we went downtown one day and we was trying to get some arrangements, because at that time I was only making introductions and endings. But inside the strain I wasn't doing it, you see.
